figures.finding: Spanish is the official language; Quechua, Aymara and the other native languages are also official where they predominate.

alsoOfficial: other native languages where they predominate

sources.said: The official languages of the State are Spanish and, wherever they predominate, Quechua, Aymara, and other native tongues

figures.finding: Lima is the capital of Peru (Cusco is the historical capital); no primary source read says where most screen work is made.

sources.said: The capital of the Republic of Peru is the city of Lima.

figures.finding: Peru's Performers Law sets no amount: it gives a performer the right to an equitable and sufficient pay, caps the working day at eight hours (48 a week) with rehearsals, make-up and preparation counted inside it, and requires a national audiovisual production to cast at least 80% Peruvian performers who take at least 60% of the cast payroll; films are governed by their own law.
figures.applies: Peru; Ley 28131 del Artista Intérprete y Ejecutante, as amended up to Legislative Decree 1451 (WIPO Lex consolidation); Ley 32409 not read.

sources.said: El artista y/o el trabajador técnico vinculado a la actividad artística tiene derecho a una remuneración equitativa y suficiente como retribución por su trabajo. … La Jornada ordinaria de trabajo para varones y mujeres mayores de edad es de ocho horas diarias o cuarenta y ocho horas semanales como máximo. … Toda producción audiovisual artística nacional deberá estar conformada como mínimo por un 80% de artistas nacionales. … Las producciones cinematográficas se rigen por su propia legislación.

No body for stage directors was found to try; no fee, minimum or agreement for items 7, 8 or 9

Result: Ley 28131 read: "Artículo 32º.- Remuneración 32.1 El artista y/o el trabajador técnico vinculado a la actividad artística tiene derecho a una remuneración equitativa y suficiente como retribución por su trabajo"; article 18 gives a "remuneración equitativa" for uses of performances, article 31 the working day; no amount, minimum or per-performance rate for actors, and nothing for stage directors as such. D.Leg. 822 (original 1996 text, later amended): only its first page was read; a law sets no playwright fee in any page read, and no tariff for dramatic works was found at APDAYC (institution)
